q: Fluid is a substance that offers no permanent resistance to deforming forces.
e: True. Fluid is a substance that offers no permanent resistance to deforming forces. A fluid yields steadily under shear; it does not keep a fixed shape.

q: Fluid statics concentrates on fluids in motion, while fluid dynamics concerns with the fluids at rest.
e: False. Fluid statics studies fluids at rest. The error is the part about Fluid statics concentrates fluids motion dynamics.

q: Motion of fluids can be classified by two types, laminar flow and turbulent flow.
e: True. Motion of fluids can be classified by two types, laminar flow and turbulent flow. Laminar flow moves in smooth layers with no mixing between neighbouring sheets.

q: If fluid particles are moving steady in smooth paths in layers, with each layer moving smoothly past the adjacent layers with no mixing, such a flow is called turbulent flow.
e: False. Smooth layered motion with no mixing is laminar flow, not turbulent flow. The error is the part about fluid particles moving steady smooth paths.

q: In this steady laminar flow, streamlines do not cross each other.
e: True. In this steady laminar flow, streamlines do not cross each other. A streamline is the path a fluid particle follows. In steady laminar flow, streamlines do not cross.

q: Every fluid particle arriving at a given point has a different velocity in steady laminar flow.
e: False. In steady laminar flow every particle arriving at a given point has the same velocity. The error is the part about Every fluid particle arriving given point.

q: If the flow or path of the fluid particles are irregular, their direction is always changing or whirling, this fluid movement is called turbulent flow.
e: True. If the flow or path of the fluid particles are irregular, their direction is always changing or whirling, this fluid movement is called turbulent flow. Turbulent flow is irregular and whirling, so speed and direction at a point keep changing.

q: In turbulent flow the speed of the fluid at a point is continuously undergoing changes in both magnitude and direction.
e: True. In turbulent flow the speed of the fluid at a point is continuously undergoing changes in both magnitude and direction. Turbulent flow is irregular and whirling, so speed and direction at a point keep changing.

q: The volume of a gas depends on pressure and temperature obeying Boyle's law and Charles' law.
e: True. The volume of a gas depends on pressure and temperature obeying Boyle's law and Charles' law. Gas volume depends on p and T through Boyle and Charles.

q: The volume of a liquid depends heavily on pressure if the temperature is constant.

q: Ideal laminar fluid flow considers the fluid is compressible.

q: Ideal laminar fluid flow considers the flow has no friction or friction is neglected.
e: True. Ideal laminar fluid flow considers the flow has no friction or friction is neglected. Laminar flow moves in smooth layers with no mixing between neighbouring sheets.

q: Internal friction in fluids is called viscosity.
e: True. Internal friction in fluids is called viscosity. Viscosity is shear stress divided by velocity gradient, η = (F/A)/(dv/dy).

q: Ideal laminar fluid flow considers high viscosity.
e: False. Ideal Bernoulli flow is non-viscous, so internal friction is neglected. The error is the part about Ideal laminar fluid flow considers high.

e: True. Ideal laminar fluid flow considers the fluid flow is laminar (steady) and turbulent flow is not taken into account. Laminar flow moves in smooth layers with no mixing between neighbouring sheets.
